name: GROUP
question: Is supervised group-based pelvic floor muscle training noninferior to individual training for older women with stress or mixed urinary incontinence?

design.population: 362 community-dwelling women aged 60 years or older with stress or mixed urinary incontinence and at least three leakage episodes weekly.
design.locator: Full text, Methods—Design and Participants; Results—Trial Participants

verdictNote: The per-protocol confidence limit excluded the prespecified 10-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: Among 319 of 362 randomized older women with stress or mixed urinary incontinence who completed one-year follow-up, supervised group-based pelvic floor muscle training was noninferior to individual training for one-year reduction in diary-recorded leakage episodes (74% versus 70% median reduction).

reports.label: One-year clinical outcomes
reports.citation: Dumoulin C, Morin M, Danieli C, et al. "Group-Based vs Individual Pelvic Floor Muscle Training to Treat Urinary Incontinence in Older Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Intern Med.* 2020;180(10):1284-1293. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2020.2993

results.measure: One-year median percentage reduction in seven-day diary episodes; difference in percentage points, individual minus group; per protocol
results.note: 154/178 group and 165/184 individual participants completed one-year follow-up (319 total). The upper confidence limit of 7 points excluded the prespecified 10-point noninferiority margin; reported P=.58 tests a between-group difference.
results.locator: Full text, Results—Primary Outcome and Figure 2; Methods—Statistical Analysis

results.measure: One-year median percentage reduction; difference in percentage points, individual minus group; intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis
results.note: Last observation carried forward for participants without one-year assessments; upper confidence limit remained below the 10-point margin.
results.locator: Full text, Methods—Statistical Analysis; Results—Primary Outcome and Figure 2

results.measure: Much or very much better at 1 year
results.locator: Full text, Results—Secondary Outcomes and Table 2

results.measure: Reported no need for other treatment at 1 year
results.locator: Full text, Results—Secondary Outcomes and Table 2

harms.label: Minor adverse events

values.individual: 27 women: 21 with vaginal discomfort and 6 with spotting

harms.note: Individual-arm symptoms occurred during intravaginal biofeedback; events were mainly in the first two sessions and resolved without treatment.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: No serious adverse events were reported in either arm.

delivery.label: Supervised training protocol
delivery.value: After one individual contraction-teaching session, both arms received 12 weekly one-hour sessions with 15 minutes of education and 45 minutes of exercise; group sessions included eight women.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods—Interventions; PubMed abstract, Interventions

delivery.label: Arm-specific support
delivery.value: Individual sessions included 10–15 minutes of intravaginal EMG biofeedback; 12/166 group participants completing treatment (7%) requested a 20-minute private contraction check.

delivery.label: Home exercise and attendance
delivery.value: Home exercises were prescribed five days weekly during treatment and three days weekly for the following nine months; mean attendance was 11.4/12 group and 11.7/12 individual sessions.

delivery.label: Other incontinence care by one year
delivery.note: Reported professional visits, medication, or other treatment despite a request to refrain during follow-up.

reports.label: One-year economic analysis
reports.citation: Cacciari LP, Kouakou CRC, Poder TG, et al. "Group-based pelvic floor muscle training is a more cost-effective approach to treat urinary incontinence in older women: economic analysis of a randomised trial." *J Physiother.* 2022;68(3):191-196. doi:10.1016/j.jphys.2022.06.001
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Design and Outcome measures

results.measure: One-year cost difference per woman, group minus individual, 2019 Canadian dollars
results.note: Economic evaluation alongside the 362-person randomized trial; absolute arm costs were not reported in the abstract.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, Participants, Outcome measures, Results

results.measure: One-year cost difference per woman, group minus individual, 2019 Canadian dollars
results.note: The abstract reports group training was at least 60% less costly across the perspectives studied.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Outcome measures and Results
